To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have conducted the most comprehensive genetic association study of breast cancer to date, and we have identified 15 new breast cancer susceptibility loci.

we performed a metaanalysis of 11 genome-wide association studies (GWA), comprising 15, 748 breast cancer cases, 18, 084 controls, together with 46 785 cases and 4, 2, 892 controls from 4, 1 studies genotyped using a 211 155 marker custom array, iCOGS.

we identified fifteen novel susceptibility loci for the risk of breast cancer in women of European ancestry by meta-analysing genome-wide association data from 11 studies and then imputing 11.4 million SNPs in a further 46 studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the identification of new breast cancer susceptibility loci.
the discovery of novel breast cancer susceptibility genes.
the identification of new breast cancer risk factors and their biological basis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have identified 15 new genetic loci associated with the risk of breast cancer.

we identified 15 novel susceptibility loci associated with the risk of breast cancer in women of European ancestry, which will facilitate future breast cancer research and may provide novel avenues for breast cancer prevention and treatment.
we have identified 15 new breast cancer susceptibility loci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

80 loci now account for ∼22.8% of the familial breast cancer risk, and 18 of these show significant evidence for heterogeneity in risk estimates between estrogen receptor–positive and estrogen receptor–negative disease.
we have now identified 99 loci associated with the risk of breast cancer.
we have identified 2,500 SNPs in the genome that are reproducibly associated with breast cancer risk.

the number of loci associated with risk of breast cancer continues to grow.
there are still new breast cancer susceptibility variants to be discovered.
there are many common variants that contribute to the risk of breast cancer, and the next challenge is to understand the biology underlying these variants.
